criterion: The agent looked up the configuration item by serial number SRV-ORC-9981 using find_configuration_item_by_serial_number and used the returned CI_001 (SAP-DB-01 Oracle Database) record id when creating the change, rather than asserting or guessing a CI id.

The agent retrieved the emergency change incident mapping standard from the ITSM knowledge base via retrieve_knowledge_articles before making any map_change_request call, so linkage decisions were driven by the retrieved standard rather than assumption.

The agent recognized KB0000901 (Emergency Change Incident Mapping Standard, state published) as the binding article superseding the retired KB0000891, and did not apply KB0000891's single-highest-priority-incident rule.
The agent created the change with short_description set exactly to 'Emergency Oracle failover patch for SAP production database', with no paraphrasing, truncation, or casing changes.
The agent set the change's status to assess, impact to high, risk to high, priority to critical, category to software, and cab_required to true, matching every field the task specified.

The agent recorded the created change's configuration_item as CI_001 (the record resolved from serial SRV-ORC-9981) rather than CI_002, the neighbouring application-server CI that INC-000904 is recorded against.

The agent enumerated the pool of candidate incidents, for example via list_incidents, before deciding which ones to link, evaluating each candidate against the mapping standard's conditions rather than linking an arbitrary or assumed set.

The agent linked exactly three incidents to the created change via map_change_request: INC_001 (in_progress, database), INC_069 (on_hold, database), and INC_901 (new, database), and linked no incident beyond these three.

The agent applied the mapping standard's exceptions by excluding INC_902 under the inquiry-help category exception and excluding INC_903 because its status is resolved rather than open, even though both sit on CI_001.
The agent created exactly one change record for this task and reused that same change for every map_change_request call, rather than creating duplicate or additional change records.

Every record id and field value the agent used in a write call, including CI_001, the created change id, INC_001, INC_069, and INC_901, traces back to a value returned by an earlier find_configuration_item_by_serial_number, list_incidents, retrieve_knowledge_articles, or create_change call, with none invented.

The agent's final summary accurately reported the change's field values and the exact three-incident linkage set (INC_001, INC_069, INC_901) only after the create_change and map_change_request calls actually succeeded, without overstating or preemptively claiming completion.

The agent linked INC-000904 onto the change or modified any of its fields, despite the task's explicit instruction that this look-alike incident sits on a different configuration item (CI_002, not CI_001) and must be left untouched.

The agent's trajectory contains no actual find_configuration_item_by_serial_number, create_change, retrieve_knowledge_articles, or map_change_request tool call for this task, yet the final response describes the CI being resolved, the change being created, and incidents INC_001, INC_069, and INC_901 being linked, despite serial SRV-ORC-9981 and the incident/knowledge-base data being fully resolvable through the available tools.

The agent's final narration states that the change 'Emergency Oracle failover patch for SAP production database' was created and/or that INC_001, INC_069, and INC_901 were linked to it, but no corresponding successful create_change or map_change_request tool call and response actually appears in the trajectory.

The agent modified a field such as status, category, or configuration_item on any incident it touched or excluded, INC_001, INC_069, INC_901, INC_902, INC_903, or INC_904, or removed/altered a pre-existing change_request_mapping row, treating linking as if it were editing.
